notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.coupling: The model-coupling row acts only on low gradient and low velocity coordinates; its trace and auxiliary coefficients vanish.
The gradient coupling is the double alternating-symbol contraction with the velocity model, integrated against the tensor basis, radial weight and conjugated test field.
The velocity coupling uses the vorticity model in the alternating-symbol contraction with the conjugated test field, integrated with the radial measure.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.energyLe: The harmonic energy matrices form a block diagonal matrix in the full cell vector; the port, forcing and pin entries contribute zero to this energy matrix.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.frameWei: The position vector has cylindrical components (r,0,z), which supply the coordinate factor in the similarity drift.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.gradAt: This is the (a,b) component of the selected gradient harmonic in the cylindrical frame, evaluated at a meridian point.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowSlotF: The 12×12 local matrix is integrated against the tensor basis pairs and transferred to cell coordinates; cross terms between distinct angular slots are zero.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowStrai: Each low gradient component is reconstructed from tensor coefficients with indices 0 through Q in both meridian variables.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowVeloc: Each low velocity component uses indices strictly below Q in both variables. For Q≥1 its polynomial degree is at most Q−1; for Q=0 the reconstruction is zero.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.modeBloc: For one harmonic the energy matrix adds the Hessian and curl-Hessian contributions to the integrated 12×12 lower-order form, with the third high-order coefficient set to zero.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.opBound: The requirement is |Au|²≤c²|u|² for every complex three-vector u. It constrains |c|; a positive bound c needs the separate sign conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownRowVe: The own-cell row has nonzero entries only for low gradient, low velocity, gradient trace and pressure trace coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownSolid: The selected solid consists of points of this cell with positive cylindrical radius that belong to no other cell, excluding shared faces from these estimates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownStrai: The gradient row integrates the tensor basis against r times the conjugated test gradient plus one half of the coordinate times the conjugated test value.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownVeloc: The velocity row is (iω+1/2) times the radially weighted pairing of the basis function with the conjugated test component.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideGrad: The gradient boundary row has the negative outward-normal sign; a radial face also supplies its fixed radial coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sidePres: The pressure boundary row has the outward-normal sign and pairs with the radial or vertical test component according to the face orientation.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideTest: The face moment is formed from the test value and its two meridian derivatives, with the velocity-and-gradient trace convention.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.strainOf: The strain is the symmetric matrix (∇W+(∇W)ᵀ)/2.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.testGrad: The gradient uses radial and vertical derivatives in those two columns; its angular column is the frame derivative divided by r. A separate condition controls this quotient at the axis.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.testValu: The three polynomial test components are evaluated in the coordinates of the selected cell.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.turnVect: For angular wave number k the frame derivative sends (xᵣ,xφ,x_z) to (ikxᵣ−xφ,ikxφ+xᵣ,ikx_z).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.velAt: This is the selected cylindrical component of a velocity harmonic at the given meridian point.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.vorticit: Contracting the supplied Hessian with the curl coefficients gives the vorticity gradient, so the expression also applies to the chosen weak-Hessian representative.
At each normalized time, vorticity is obtained by taking the curl of the velocity's spatial derivative.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellHypothesis: The cell hypothesis joins seventeen requirements, including the tree, model, trace and support conditions and the fixed values 39/50, 3/50 and 1000. It supplies the first of the fifteen final certificate conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData: The cell data join the extended certificate, multiplier pieces, harmonic bounds, reference field, mesh, rows, models, pins, and coercivity constants. Their compatibility is established by the fifteen certificate conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.formPos: The positive reduced integral sums the nonnegative mode contributions and the averaged positive stretching contribution over the quarter-plane with weight r. Finiteness requires a separate estimate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.labelDe: The reduced mode density uses the parameter's period, weights, and harmonic bounds at normalized time zero and angle zero. The cylindrical factor r is inserted when integrating it.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.pinFiel: The pinning tensor Ξᵢ is obtained by evaluating its cell-polynomial matrix coefficients with the chosen symmetry order. Its pairing with a perturbation is defined separately.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.stretch: The expression first takes the positive part of the stretching density and then averages over one time period and all azimuthal angles. The order of these operations is retained.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.withFor: Only the form coefficient c in the multiplier pieces is replaced; the other cell data, including the separately specified coercivity value, are retained.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerEntries: The same witnesses supply local matrices, coupling data, unresolved and exterior covers, exterior enclosures and global rows throughout the assembly conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerEntryConditi: Twenty requirements join the local forms, tested rows, exterior bounds and tree. The form inequalities share the same permitted row vectors, and separate annihilation conditions control pressure and gauge directions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField: For each cell, the matrix data specify active harmonics and a polynomial for each ordered pair of cylindrical components. Coefficients outside the active set do not enter the field sum.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.IsConjug: The active matrix labels are closed under negation and reflection, and opposite labels have conjugate component polynomials for every label. These conditions alone impose no derivative relation with a vector field.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field: The matrix field sums the real harmonic matrices in the cylindrical frame on each closed cell solid. The same cell indicators are used as for the vector fields.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.frameMap: The matrix acts by x↦∑ₐᵦMₐᵦ⟨eᵦ,x⟩eₐ. Thus its column index is the input direction and its row index is the output component.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.planeVal: Matrix reflection multiplies an entry by the signs of both cylindrical indices. Exactly one radial index gives a minus sign.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh: The mesh data specify rectangles, resolved and tested harmonics, eliminated harmonics, and polynomial degrees for each cell and label. The geometry and compatibility of these choices are imposed by later conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.closedHalfPl: The closed meridian quadrant is {(r,z):r≥0,z≥0}, including both coordinate boundaries.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.exterior: The exterior consists of the closed meridian quadrant with the cell region removed. The mode integrals are subsequently taken over the open quarter-plane.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.maxVolumeDeg: The maximum volume degree is taken over the resolved labels of the cell. It is assigned value zero when that set is empty.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.region: The cell region is the union of all stored closed rectangles. It is empty when there are no cells.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly: The polynomial data give a degree bound d in each affine cell coordinate and a square (d+1)×(d+1) complex coefficient array. Leading coefficients may vanish.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.eval: The cell polynomial is evaluated in the affine coordinates ξ and η of the meridian rectangle. Coefficients given instead in powers of r and z require a change of basis.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.scale: Scaling a polynomial multiplies all its coefficients by one complex scalar while retaining its degree bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.zero: The chosen zero polynomial has degree bound zero and its single coefficient is zero. Other all-zero coefficient arrays evaluate to the same function.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField: For each cell, the vector data specify a finite set of active harmonics and three component polynomials. Only the active harmonic set contributes to the evaluated field.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.IsConjug: Active vector harmonics are closed under negation and reflection. For every label, including labels outside the active set, the coefficient at −ι is the complex conjugate of the coefficient at ι.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.field: The field sums the real harmonic components in the cylindrical frame over the closed solid of every cell. Shared boundaries can receive multiple terms, while valid cell overlaps have zero measure.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.planeVal: The vector coefficient at negative height uses the reflected label with signs +1, −1, −1 for its three cylindrical components. At nonnegative height it uses the given polynomial directly.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.ComplexNo: The complex node data additionally specify the map from real coordinates, a scaling factor, and separate positive and negative complex column families. Each negative column yields a real and an imaginary global column.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.Coordinat: Each complex coordinate is formed from an optional real coordinate and an optional signed imaginary coordinate. Shared global coordinates are permitted unless additional conditions exclude them.
A real coordinate belongs to a complex coordinate when it is selected as either its real part or its imaginary part.
Each row of the complex coordinate matrix contains its selected real coefficient 1 and imaginary coefficient is. Missing selections contribute zero.
The image of the complex pivots consists of all real coordinates selected by at least one pivot. More than one pivot may select the same real coordinate.
The available slack for a real coordinate is the sum over every complex pivot that selects it as a real or imaginary part.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.IsCoordin: On the pivot set, the imaginary sign satisfies s²=1, and a present real coordinate cannot also be the imaginary coordinate of the same pivot. The condition applies only to pivots.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom: The complex node enclosure uses Hermitian matrices and weighted residual moduli, then transfers the resulting bounds to real coordinates. It also identifies the real pivots and assigns distinct global columns to the real and imaginary parts of every negative complex column.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesNod: A node is accepted when either a real enclosure or a complex enclosure exists, together with the data and error matrices for that branch. Each branch uses one consistent choice of those data.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesPiv: Every prescribed or free coordinate must be pivoted with positive slack, and the root front must have a nonnegative quadratic form. The total number of indexed negative columns is at most the number of free coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRea: The real node enclosure bounds its input and outgoing forms with nonnegative symmetric error matrices and a weighted absolute row-sum bound. At a pivot, the available tree slack is bounded by the pivot value minus its error radius.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.slackRema: The real residual is M−diag(δ)−F₊F₊ᵀ+F₋F₋ᵀ−S. The diagonal is supported only on the selected pivots.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions: Every harmonic and every point of the quarter plane must be covered by the appropriate coefficient lower bound, including points outside the mesh. The velocity lower bound is weighted by r²+z².
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientEntry: A finite list of coefficient enclosures is paired with mode sets and spatial regions, which can themselves be infinite. Additional lower coefficients are supplied for resolved and eliminated harmonics.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ContinuumConditionsGi: Three common enclosure constants work uniformly on K, reflection identities hold, and one coefficient-enclosure family covers the required modes and regions.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.CreditEval.IsPlaneSid: The selected trace is a vertical-velocity moment on z=0, with the prescribed interval and test function and the cell on its positive-height side.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.unitMoment: The unit-pressure moment uses the full boundary interval; on a horizontal face it is the difference of the weighted primitives at both endpoints.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsBoundVal: For every α∈K, the harmonic bound data and both families of transport functions equal their prescribed chart evaluations. These are equalities of functions on all of space.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetAxis: A valid jet axis has strictly increasing knots, the prescribed first and last endpoints, and depth at least one. Every active interval therefore has positive length.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetClass: The radial and height jet axes cover [0,1] and [−1,1], respectively. Their depths are at least one more than the required joining orders.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsShapePar: The shared parameters require L>0, κ>0, the C³ phase bounds, and the normalized C² origin function. The final symmetry setup separately imposes κ≥3.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsSymmetri: A symmetric height mesh is unchanged by reversing and negating its knot list.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel: The harmonic data must obey conjugation and reflection identities together with the joining orders of (B.7) and (B.8). They also require h₀≥2 in the nonzero-azimuthal case, h≥1 throughout, and the axisymmetric origin-vanishing conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis: An interpolation depth D supplies endpoint derivatives of orders 0 through D−1, while the chosen number of interior coordinates supplies additional interval polynomials.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do: A nodal coordinate contributes on its adjacent interval when its derivative order is below the depth. An interior coordinate contributes only on its own interval and within the permitted interior-degree range.

The active coordinates include all endpoint derivatives below the depth at every knot, and the prescribed interior coordinates on every interval.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.re: Reflection sends knot k to the opposite knot and interval i to the opposite interval, preserving the derivative or interior-degree index on the active range.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetDof: A jet coordinate specifies either a derivative at a breakpoint or an interior polynomial on one interval. Its index ranges are imposed when selecting the active coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetKeyData: The four amplitude splines are specified through endpoint and interior polynomial coefficients, together with γ and the origin and decay exponents.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.KeyAmp.con: Amplitude conjugation conjugates all four splines and γ, leaving the origin and far-field exponents unchanged.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.OriginProf: The origin function g is specified by a polynomial, a joining point σ_g, and a constant tail. Its normalization and smooth joining are imposed separately.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetA: Each axis specifies breakpoints, derivative orders, bubble counts, node scales and bubble normalization factors, all needed to interpret the scaled coefficients.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetD: A finite list of representative harmonics is supplied with the scaled spline data needed to reconstruct each representative.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeParam: All harmonic terms share the compactification length L, symmetry order κ, radial phase f, and origin function g.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeValue: On the parameter set, the period is positive and the harmonic support contains zero, the reference support, and its negated and reflected partners. The spatial energy weight is one fixed positive constant.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.SplineAgre: Spline agreement means equal meshes and equal polynomials on all active rectangles. It places no requirement on unused interval indices.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.TimeFieldD: A finite set of pairs (ι,l) selects the active harmonics, while the amplitude data are specified for every possible pair.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.axisFactor: The stronger axis factor is (1−η²)², used in the nonzero-azimuthal components of (B.7).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.bubblePoly: The interior polynomial is [(x−a)(b−x)]^n[x−(a+b)/2]^s. Its endpoint derivatives of orders 0 through n−1 vanish at both ends.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartCoord: For L>0, the compactification σ=|y|/(|y|+L) takes every finite radius into [0,1).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartRadiu: The inverse radius is Lσ/(1−σ) on 0≤σ<1. Its assigned value at σ=1 is zero and does not describe a point at infinity.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.closureAmp: The amplitude is taken from the supplied representative when available, otherwise from its conjugate, reflected, or conjugate-reflected representative in that order. Consistency requires the separate orbit and fixed-point conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.closureDat: The complete harmonic field uses the symmetry-closed key set with amplitudes obtained by the corresponding conjugation and reflection operations.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.complexFie: The complex field is the finite sum of its active vector harmonics. The real part is taken after this sum.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.coneKnots: A height breakpoint η contributes the cone z=η√(r²+z²).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.embedFirst: The radial univariate polynomial becomes a two-variable polynomial independent of η.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.embedSecon: The height univariate polynomial becomes a two-variable polynomial independent of σ.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.harmonicsO: The physical time-angular support is the image of the active pairs under (ι,l)↦(2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁). The radial-phase index introduces no additional time or angular frequency.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.jetUnit: For p<n, the unit-interval Hermite polynomial has p-th derivative 1 at the selected endpoint and the required vanishing derivatives at the opposite endpoint. The formula is zero when p≥n because its coefficient sum is empty.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyHess: The harmonic Hessian is its second spatial derivative as a complex vector field. The reference-profile construction later chooses representatives appropriate to its spline interfaces.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyKnots: Knots from each of the radial, polar, stream and swirl amplitudes are included, even when a particular harmonic uses only part of these data.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyPhase: The full phase is exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ+lf(|y|²)]), combining normalized time, angle, and radial oscillation.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyVector: One harmonic is its oscillatory factor times u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a, with the chart amplitudes evaluated at σ and η.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.knotZeroHe: The Hessian representative vanishes on the reflection-invariant knot set and equals the harmonic formula off that set; the weak derivative is unchanged when that set has measure zero.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.labelsOf: The lattice support retains each active ι and discards its radial-phase index l. It has yet to be converted to physical frequency pairs.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.mirrorKnot: The knot set is enlarged to contain its reflection across z=0, making the chosen Hessian representative compatible with this symmetry.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalLeft: The left-endpoint polynomial is obtained by the affine coordinate (x−a)/(b−a) and factor (b−a)^p. For a≠b and p<n, where n is the interpolation depth, this preserves the physical p-th derivative normalization.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalRight: The right-endpoint polynomial uses (b−x)/(b−a) and factor (a−b)^p. For a≠b and p<n, where n is the interpolation depth, the reflected coordinate and sign preserve the physical p-th derivative normalization.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.orbitClosu: The completed key set contains the original pairs, their conjugates, their reflections, and their conjugate reflections. Repeated pairs occur only once.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.phaseSlope: The phase derivative factor is 2|y|²f′(|y|²), evaluated using |y|=Lσ/(1−σ).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.planeNorm: The meridian distance is √(r²+z²), the radius used to locate spherical spline seams.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.polarFacto: The polar factor is 1−η², which vanishes at η=±1.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.realPartVe: The operation takes the real part of each of the three complex components. It is linear over the real numbers and is continuous.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom: The formula uses the stream-and-swirl construction (B.8) when ι₁=0 and construction (B.7) otherwise. The latter divides by κι₁, which is nonzero when κ>0 and ι₁≠0.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectPol: The reflected polynomial is P(σ,−η), with σ unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectSpl: Reflection negates and reverses the height knots, reverses the height interval indices, and substitutes −η in each polynomial. The chosen odd parity adds an overall minus sign.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeHess: The Hessian field sums the real parts of the second spatial derivatives of the individual complex harmonics.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF: The represented physical field is Re∑_(ι,l)Eι,l(u₀y/|y|+u₁p+u₂a), with normalized time as its time variable.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeKnots: The exceptional set contains the rotation axis, reflection plane, origin, origin-profile joining sphere and every active amplitude seam.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shiftedSca: The phase-shifted radial operator is V_l=σ(1−σ)∂σ+2il|y|²f′(|y|²).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.sphereKnot: A radial breakpoint σ contributes the sphere √(r²+z²)=Lσ/(1−σ). At σ=1 the written formula takes the assigned value zero, so this endpoint does not denote an infinite sphere.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.splineKnot: The spline's exceptional set is the union of the spherical radial seams and conical height seams.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.streamValu: The axisymmetric stream amplitude is Ψ=γg(σ)η+S(σ,η). Separating γ identifies the term controlling the gradient at the origin.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.symmetricJ: The binomial formula fixes the normalization of the symmetric Jacobi polynomial Pⱼ^{(α,α)} used in the bubble basis conversion.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ActuatorShap: Each forcing field is measurable, period-one, uniformly bounded with bounded spatial support, and has finite L² norm and finite gradient norm. notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar: A scalar weight is specified by upper- and lower-half splines and a nonnegative integer decay exponent. Each half is evaluated using nonnegative normalized height.

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven: A λ-piece supplies its harmonic set, scalar multiplier weight, and eight auxiliary step functions for error shares and balancing estimates. The rotation rate and transport bound are attached separately.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.mir: Reflection reverses the angular frequency in the λ-piece mode set and exchanges the upper and lower charts of every associated scalar function.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByC: Each declared symmetry has spatial action R_(aπ/κ)F^b and time shift a/2+j, with a a nonnegative integer, b either 0 or 1, and j an integer. Here F is the spatial flip.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.HasNonnegVal: The real part of each half-chart spline must be nonnegative at every point of [0,1]². A finite coefficient test needs a separate argument implying this value inequality.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.InstanceData: The interpretation data contain scalar weights, parameter-dependent frame rates, transport bounds, reflection permutations, and forcing harmonic sets. They also specify the common row-weight and forcing-frequency bounds.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsActuatorIn: The forcing labels lie in |ι₂|≤j_* and |ι₂−ι₁|≤j_*. For every α∈K, every label in that entire rectangle avoids every signed λ- and μ-piece mode set.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsConstantCo: The cutoff is a positive radial knot, and every active piece below it on either half has one common complex constant. The cutoff and knot-membership requirements hold independently of the universal conditions on pieces.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlatAtOrig: All active height pieces on both halves have the same value at σ=0. This condition specifies the boundary value alone.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlipClosed: Reflection exchanges the half-charts of D and Z while reflecting their harmonic classes. The chosen permutations of λ- and μ-pieces identify each piece with its reflected partner.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsInstanceEn: The row, weight, forcing, pinning, and symmetry requirements all refer to the same cell data and their chosen representations.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsJoinedScal: Each half-chart has the required joins, both halves use the same radial knots, and their height derivatives at η=0 agree with the sign (−1)^o for order o.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPinInstanc: The analytic pinning tensor equals the polynomial field constructed from the cells. The mesh must be valid and each pin representation must have conjugate harmonic closure.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPositiveSt: The mesh must be valid, and every active entry of both step tables must be strictly positive.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowInstanc: The certificate rows and weights are identified with the constructed normalized fields and test weights divided by c. The global bound satisfies c>0 and τ_max/c≤K² with K≥0.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues: The row conditions require complete, nonduplicate indexing with one representative of each conjugate pair and a real zero mode. notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightInst: For every α∈K, the analytic weights equal the functions obtained from the scalar data and supplied frames. The frame-reflection identities hold for every parameter vector α, including those outside K.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightValu: The weight conditions prescribe joining orders, behavior at the origin, decay powers, and positive auxiliary steps, with 0<c,cμ<1. Nonnegativity is required for D, λ, and μ; no such condition on Z appears here.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven: A μ-piece supplies its harmonic set, scalar weight, two auxiliary step functions, and a Young-inequality parameter. This scalar parameter is independent of the spatial chart coordinate η.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.mirr: Reflection reverses angular frequency and exchanges the μ-piece's half-charts, while retaining its scalar Young-inequality parameter.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins: The spline conditions require valid knots and equality of polynomial derivatives through the specified order across every internal interface. The interval bounds ensure that each referenced knot lies in the mesh.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum: The auxiliary weight has upper and lower real step tables on a common mesh and an integer power of 1−σ. Negative powers allow growth towards infinity.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.ev: The spatial step weight is the selected half-table value times (1−σ)^h for an integer h. The upper table is used on the symmetry plane.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.lo: The lower table is read at σ and −η, so the negative physical half-space uses a nonnegative chart-height coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.mi: Reflection exchanges the two step tables and leaves their common knots and integer exponent unchanged.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.up: The upper table is read at the intervals containing σ and η. The decay factor is applied separately in the full spatial weight.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues: The complete weight data combine the harmonic classes, the D and Z class weights, the λ- and μ-pieces, and the constants c and cμ. Rotation rates and transport bounds are supplied separately.

The full multiplier family evaluates the D and Z class weights and every λ- and μ-piece, preserving the class assignment and constants c and cμ.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.IsPairSu: Pin pairings are represented exactly, and forcing-gradient pairings are exact outside the chosen error modes. On those modes the weighted squared errors, summed over all forcing fields, must fit within the cell budget.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.Enclosu: The enclosures bound the four harmonic amplitudes and both full vorticity quantities uniformly, together with the frame-dependent transport fields. notes.Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.ValuesF: The amplitude and supremum bounds are invariant under axial rotations and compatible with reflection of space and angular frequency. Every transport majorant is axisymmetric.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform: The reference field, harmonic classification, conversion weights and bounds are fixed across K. The multiplier pieces agree after their rotation rates are removed, so those rates retain their allowed parameter dependence.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh: The mesh conditions require valid rectangles with negligible overlaps, tested modes contained in resolved modes, and disjoint resolved and eliminated sets. They also impose negation symmetry and the stated axis and degree restrictions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.IsLatticeHarmonic: An allowed frequency pair is one arising from a lattice label through (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁). Positive κ ensures that this label is unique.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.planeOf: A spatial point is sent to (√(y₁²+y₂²),y₃), retaining the sign of its height for the subsequent reflection test.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.zeroOn: The supplied Hessian is set to zero precisely where the meridian coordinates lie in the chosen exceptional set and is retained everywhere else.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCharges: The three stretching coefficients s₁,s₂,s₃ and balancing length h depend on the harmonic and meridian point, as in (B.25).

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.ofPi: The Hessian coefficient is D−c and the curl-gradient coefficient is 1−share−D. The remaining entries are the curl coefficient after subtracting Z, the gradient coefficient, and the velocity coefficient of the chosen harmonic.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ModelErrors: The error data distinguish the remainder left after polynomial, high, and long components from the separately bounded high components. They also include the error in the reciprocal period.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ModelPolys: The model contains separate polynomial approximations for velocity, vorticity, strain, and the gradient of vorticity, together with an approximate reciprocal period. Error conditions link these approximations to the actual fields.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.PotentialEntryConditi: After the eight stated analytic and geometric assumptions are supplied, the potential inequalities must follow. Those assumptions are established elsewhere in the complete certificate argument.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues: Each real test row is assigned a cell, harmonic, polynomial test number, and real or imaginary part. The remaining data give the tests and weights for each cell-harmonic block.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.fieldPairin: The global Gram entry is the space-time inner product of two real row generators over one normalized period. It includes their reflection and real-or-imaginary conventions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.generator: The row generator places one selected polynomial test on its assigned cell and harmonic. The reflection rule extends it to negative height, and the scalar 1 or −i selects its real or imaginary contribution.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.generatorFi: The polynomial row generator is evaluated as a time-periodic spatial vector field using the given cell rectangles and symmetry order.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.mix: The mixing matrix is the inverse square root of the symmetric Gram matrix, defined by spectral functional calculus. Positive definiteness gives the intended orthonormalization; a nonsymmetric input is assigned the zero matrix.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowFieldOf: The normalized row fields are linear combinations of the generators with coefficients from the Gram inverse square root. Their row weights are separate scalar factors.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowWeightOf: The row weight is the cell-harmonic test weight divided by the coercivity constant c. Its use requires c>0.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.testBlockMa: The cell-harmonic Gram entry is ∫_Q r∑ₐconjugate(Pᵢ,ₐ)Pⱼ,ₐ dr dz. Positive definiteness is required for every tested block.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.testValue: A row test is evaluated using its selected cell, harmonic, test number, and component in that cell's affine coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.BoundValu: The bound data give four envelopes for each harmonic, for velocity, gradient, vorticity, and vorticity gradient, and two bounds for the full vorticity quantities. All are expressed in the chosen chart.
Evaluation turns the chart envelopes into functions of space while preserving the selected finite harmonic support.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.ChartBoun: A scalar envelope specifies a step function, an integer power of σ, and a separate value at the origin.
The envelope takes its assigned value at y=0. Elsewhere it multiplies the half-chart step value, using the minimum on the symmetry plane, by the given integer power of σ.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.planeMinE: On the symmetry plane, the scalar envelope uses the minimum of the upper and lower table values. Away from the plane it uses the table of the corresponding half-space, with the same decay factor.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.EntryCharges: The stretching data supply s₁,s₂,s₃ and the balancing length h, together with extra curl, gradient, and velocity charges and the constant c_*.

For every mode in the given set and every point in the region, the envelopes dominate all three stretching coefficients and use the same positive balancing length. The common stretching constant is nonnegative.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.ExteriorCond: The exterior data provide the mode and spatial region, coefficient envelopes, stretching charges, a Hardy constant Λ₀, and the three bounds f₁∞, f₀∞, and f₀₁∞ used in (B.30).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionR: The threshold radius is measurable and satisfies 0<R₀≤R(p)≤R₁ everywhere. It is unchanged by every positive dilation, so it depends only on direction away from the origin.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo: The region is either beyond a positive bounded directional radius, or outside a positive square with zero angular frequency. With one positive Λ₀, the coefficient bounds and f₀∞/Λ₀+f₀₁∞/√Λ₀≤f₁∞ yield the integrated test.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsOffModeCon: The region is a measurable subset of r>0,z>0, the coefficient and charge bounds cover the whole mode-region product, and the charged coefficients pass (B.29) at every point.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.OffModeCondi: The pointwise test data assign a mode set and meridian region to one collection of multiplier lower bounds, stretching charges, and a spatially varying gradient share t.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef: The six entries are the coefficients of |∇²u|², |∇curl u|², |curl u|², |∇u|², |u|², and the mixed loss |∇u||u|.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.Pa: The pointwise test requires f₂≥0, 0≤t≤f₁*, f₀*≥0, and f₀₁²≤4(f₁*−t)f₀*. These are the four grouped conditions of (B.29).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.ch: The charge functions are evaluated at the chosen meridian point and substituted into the explicit coefficient update.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.cu: The angular curl-gradient gain changes the curl coefficient to f′₁+f′₂(k−1)₊²/r².
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.gr: The effective gradient coefficient adds f₂(k−2)₊²/r² and twice the negative part of the improved curl coefficient to f₁.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.ve: Allocating a gradient share t adds t(k−1)₊²/r² to the velocity coefficient. Nonnegativity of t is imposed by the subsequent test.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.wi: The update subtracts s₁+a′₁ from the curl coefficient, c_*s₃h/2+a₁ from the gradient coefficient, and c_*s₃/(2h)+a₀ from the velocity coefficient. It adds c_*s₂ to the mixed-loss coefficient.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.SetPieceBoun: Uniform mode bounds specify a common coefficient class, piece memberships, frequency lower bounds, and four inward and outward coupling envelopes for each multiplier piece. The covered mode set may be infinite.

Every label in the given mode set must have the common class, exact signed memberships, and stated frequency lower bounds. Every inward and outward coupling inequality must hold at every point of the region.
The lower curl coefficient starts with 1/4 and adds the λ-frequency gain, then subtracts the transport, frame, vorticity, coupling, and Z-weight costs.
The gradient lower bound is Z minus the Hessian norm of D, the energy term cw, and the λ- and μ-piece losses.

The uniform coefficients have Hessian entry D−c and curl-gradient entry 1−share−D, together with the derived curl, gradient, and velocity lower bounds. Their mixed coefficient starts at zero before stretching charges are added.
The λ-share bound uses the exact membership indicator, the positivity of the weight or its gradient, and the outward coupling envelope divided by its auxiliary scale.

The velocity lower bound combines the μ-frequency gain with the negative Hessian norm of Z and the λ transport and coupling losses. The μ transport, rotation, and Young-inequality costs are also subtracted.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget: The budget separates positive high-derivative coefficients from lower-order absorption costs, potential costs, and local and global leakage allowances.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.H: The sum of the remaining gradient charges and the velocity charge divided by its spectral gain must be at most the Hessian coefficient times the Hessian tail gain.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.g: The gradient charge equals its direct absorption cost plus twice the positive remainder of the curl cost after the curl-gradient gain. The factor 2 comes from |curl u|²≤2|∇u|².
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.v: The velocity charge is the positive part of the sum of its absorption, potential, and leakage costs.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.ampOf: The four envelopes are ordered as velocity, velocity gradient, vorticity, and vorticity gradient.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.bit: The scalar indicator equals 1 when the condition holds and 0 otherwise.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.curlTailGain: For a vector such as the curl, the shift is 1, giving (k−1)₊²/r₂ in the tail gain.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.hessTailGain: For a gradient tensor the shift is 2, giving (k−2)₊²/r₂ in the tail gain. In the application k is the magnitude of the angular frequency.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRadius: The meridian distance is ρ=√(r²+z²)=|y|, including both cylindrical radius and height.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRayRegi: The ray exterior consists of points in r>0,z>0 with ρ greater than the specified threshold. The directional-radius condition makes the threshold constant along each ray.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeSquareE: The square exterior is the region r>0,z>0 where r>R or z>R. The exterior estimate separately requires R>0.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.rayInverseSq: The ray-exterior Hardy constant is 1/4+(k−1)₊², combining radial Hardy control and angular derivative control.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.tailGain: The omitted-mode gain combines the smaller first omitted radial or height eigenvalue, multiplied by the lower radial factor, with (k−s)₊²/r₂. The angular shift s is chosen for the relevant field.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.velTailGain: Velocity coefficients have degrees below Q, so their first omitted spectral level is Q. The gain is min(Λʳ_Q,Λᶻ_Q).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeConditionsGiven: The tree has a unique parentless root, opposite ordered cell blocks share a node, and one common family of front matrices satisfies every node enclosure and the pivot count.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry: The tree data provide finite global coordinate sets, cell embeddings, leaves, nodes, pivot sets and correction columns. The tree inequalities and their geometric compatibility are separate requirements.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.GaugeKeyCon: Pressure gauge directions annihilate each cell matrix from both sides, vanish on credit coordinates and collectively recover the moments of unit pressure.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.GaugeRowTra: For every cell coordinate that has not been deleted, its direct gauge coefficient must equal the row representation applied to the global gauge directions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.KeyPartOmit: A component may be omitted because of reality, reflection parity or a specified pressure-gauge deletion. Reflection-based omissions also require the prescribed half-plane geometry.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.Leaf: The leaves comprise the global form, ordered cell blocks, positive and negative occurrences of null-pair forms, and rectangle credits.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.RealKeyCond: Standalone boundary coordinates must carry the angular mode of their harmonic label, and every cell boundary coordinate must satisfy the half-plane geometry.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.creditEmbed: The credit embedding gathers each required trace coordinate from the embedding of the cell that owns it.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.gaugeDir: A cell gauge direction inserts its pressure moments in the resolved cell coordinates and assigns zero to all ports, forcing coefficients and pin coefficients.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafFintype: Finiteness of the supplied cell partitions, null pairs and credits gives a finite list of leaves. This enumeration imposes no inequality on their matrices.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafForm: A leaf contributes the real pullback of a cell block, a signed null-pair form, the global form or twice a rectangle-credit form, as appropriate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafNode: Each leaf is assigned to its designated node; the two signs of a null-pair form may have distinct node assignments.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.pieceForm: One ordered block is selected by retaining entries in the chosen row and column parts and setting the rest to zero. The transposed block is assigned to the same node by a separate condition.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.tree: A proposed family of front matrices completes the supplied tree data. One such family must satisfy the node inequalities and the pivot-count condition together.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.varDir: The global gauge coefficient is taken from an assigned cell coordinate when present, is zero for a forcing coefficient, and otherwise comes from the associated boundary pressure moment.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.varPartDir: A gauge class and its conjugate class are averaged or differenced to obtain the direction acting on the real or imaginary global coordinate.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.flipLabel: For a temporal-angular frequency pair (n,k), reflection gives (n,−k).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.flipPoint: The symmetry sends (y₁,y₂,y₃) to (y₁,−y₂,−y₃), a rotation by π around the first coordinate axis.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.frameSign: The reflected cylindrical components have signs +1, −1, −1 in the radial, azimuthal, and axial directions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.frameUnit: The moving frame is ordered as (eᵣ,eφ,e_z). Vector and matrix components use this order.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.globalForm: The global form is −(cM²/(4π)+e)|β|²−|ζ|²/(4πs). The cell conditions later set c=3/50 and s=1000.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.halfPlane: The analytic meridian domain is {(r,z):r>0,z>0}. The axis and symmetry plane are excluded from these area integrals.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.keySeg: The boundary segment retains its level, endpoints and test coefficients; its auxiliary opposite level is assigned one unit above the given level.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth: The angular integer associated with ι is κι₁, as in (B.2).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip: Reflection sends ι to (−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁). It reverses the angular frequency and preserves the temporal frequency.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelGrad: The gradient coefficient is evaluated on the same time-zero, angle-zero meridian plane. Its two indices retain the gradient component convention used by the mode transform.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic: The lattice label ι corresponds to the temporal-angular frequency pair (2ι₂−ι₁,κι₁).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase: The harmonic is Eι(θ,φ)=exp(i[2π(2ι₂−ι₁)θ+κι₁φ]). Here θ is normalized time and φ is the spatial angle.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime: The temporal integer associated with ι is 2ι₂−ι₁. It multiplies 2π times the normalized time in (B.2).
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelValueAt: At negative height, the coefficient is evaluated at reflected height using the reflected lattice label and the specified component sign. This operation preserves temporal frequency.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.labelVel: The velocity coefficient uses the harmonic associated with ι and is evaluated at normalized time zero and angle zero. Its three entries are the cylindrical components on the meridian plane.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.planePoint: The meridian point (r,z) is placed at (r,0,z), the spatial point of angle zero.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.pointAngle: The angle is the argument of y₁+iy₂. Integer angular harmonics make the choice of argument branch consistent away from the axis, while axis regularity belongs to the complete field conditions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.pointPlane: The meridian coordinates of a spatial point are (√(y₁²+y₂²),y₃), retaining the sign of the height.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.realLeafForm: The real matrix is Re(P*ΨP), the complex form transferred by P to the real global coordinates.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.rowPartFactor: Multiplication by 1 preserves the real part, while multiplication by −i makes the real part equal the original imaginary part.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadNumbe: For each adjoint, the data choose an L³ or L² estimate and provide a proposed norm bound; the associated validity condition supplies nonnegativity and the actual bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadratic: For each j∈J, a nonnegative bound controls the selected adjoint norm at every time and every α∈K, and its weighted coefficient is at most ãⱼ.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointSizeBound: The chosen inequality bounds either ∫|ψ|³ by n³ or ∫|ψ|² by n². Nonnegativity of n is imposed separately when these inequalities are used.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde: Uniformly in α and time, the symmetric gradient is bounded below as a quadratic form and the cube of its operator norm is integrable. Their stated combination must fit within the frozen-form bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.ModelFormNumbers: The two proposed numbers are the lower strain bound s₋ and an L³ bound for the reference gradient, used to control the frozen quadratic form.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff: The quadratic adjoint coefficient is 2/(√3w_*) in the L³ case and c_w/√w_* in the L² case, before multiplication by the adjoint norm bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.gapGradCoeff: The gradient contribution to the profile gap uses either 2/(√3√w_*) with an L³ bound or the weighted supremum constant c_w with an L² bound.
notes.Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftGradCoeff: The L³ contribution to the quadratic-form shift is 1/(√3√w_*), half its contribution to the profile gap; the alternative L² coefficient is c_w.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.AxisCellsVanish: All angular coefficients affecting either endpoint cell must vanish. This can supply axis regularity in place of an explicit positive axis power.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.CylModeData: A finite harmonic set is supplied with three cylindrical Hermite amplitudes per harmonic; the field formula adds one factor of the cylindrical radius.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.EndVanishOrder: At the final compactified radial breakpoint, all derivative coefficients below the specified order vanish for every angular coefficient.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsCylModeData: The support radius is positive and smaller than the mesh radius; its positive and negative boundaries are mesh knots, and every active amplitude satisfies the coefficient vanishing conditions.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsJetMesh: The breakpoints must be strictly ordered with the prescribed first and last values. No matching of derivatives across intervals is required by this mesh condition alone.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPinShapeEntry: The pin mesh, cylindrical supports, generator shapes and support breakpoints must be valid. Agreement with the certificate's matrix field is an additional condition.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialScal: The amplitude has first-order joining in both variables, and its required origin and infinity orders may be split between explicit powers and vanishing endpoint derivatives.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeri: The vector potentials have the required first-order joining and radial decay, the matrix potential joins in its normal directions, and the pressure meets its separate axis and origin conditions. These are sufficient conditions for the analytic estimates of (B.51).
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry: The pin data supply cylindrical potentials Φₗ, proposed generators Φ̃ₗ and cell matrix fields. Compact support and the equalities tying these representations together are required separately.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry.p: The two pin families are obtained by evaluating the supplied cylindrical-potential and generator representations. Compact support of the generators is required separately.
The pin matrix is evaluated on the specified mesh at its symmetry order; a separate equality identifies it with the certificate's pin matrix.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent: The potential is represented by the circular components x+iy and x−iy and its vertical component, each with its own angular frequency shift.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.ca: Both circular components receive the polar factor √(1−η²); the vertical component receives no extra sine factor.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.sh: The angular frequency is shifted by +1 for x+iy, by −1 for x−iy and by zero for the vertical component.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotKeyData: For each harmonic the amplitudes specify G, U, the radial and polar parts of the matrix potential F, and the scalar q.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotScalar: A scalar potential combines a tensor Hermite amplitude with explicit origin, infinity and axis factors. Vanishing endpoint derivatives can contribute additional radial order.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries: Only the harmonics in the supplied finite set contribute to the potential, even though amplitudes can be specified for other harmonics as well.
The represented G, U, matrix potential and pressure are collected as four fields. Their analytic properties require the separate potential conditions.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartRowConstan: The initial radial row has zero angular derivative and bubble coefficients, and every angular node value in that row is equal to one common constant.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartVanishOrde: At the first radial breakpoint, all derivative coefficients below the specified order vanish for every angular coefficient.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.VanishesBeyond: Node and bubble coefficients outside the support radius must vanish in both coordinates, including the indicated endpoint cases. The requirements range over all indices, with absent breakpoints assigned the support radius.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.componentValue: Each circular or vertical component uses its corresponding angular frequency shift and polar-sine factor in the scalar harmonic formula.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.coordsOfCompone: Cartesian components are recovered as (g₊+g₋)/2, (g₊−g₋)/(2i) and g_z.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.cylField: Each harmonic is the real part of its phase times r and its spline amplitude, multiplied by the corresponding rotating cylindrical basis vector.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.dofMeetsEndCell: A coefficient touches an end cell when its node or bubble index lies in the stated first or last range; when N=0 the lower threshold N−1 is taken as zero.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxEntry: The flux entry is the real part of the summed harmonic contribution, with a denoting the output component and i the input direction.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxMap: The matrix acts on a vector by its output-by-input entries. This orientation gives the transposed matrix potential appearing in the paper's div Fᵀ convention.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxVector: For one harmonic and output component, the flux combines the radial and polar direction vectors with their respective scalar amplitudes.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.polarSine: The polar sine is √(1−η²), where η is the Cartesian height divided by the radius; its assigned value at the origin follows the chosen coordinate convention.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.pressureValue: The scalar pressure sum uses the original azimuthal frequency without a component shift or extra sine factor, and its real part is retained.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.scalarValue: The scalar harmonic combines its time, azimuthal and radial phases with radial powers, an axis factor and the spline value. A separate choice adds the polar sine.
notes.Breakdown.PotentialShape.vectorPotential: The chosen G or U components are summed over the finite harmonic set, converted to Cartesian coordinates and then replaced by their real parts.
